abstract: Diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs) represent a physical computing paradigm that performs machine learning tasks by programming the propagation of light through a series of engineered diffractive layers. By harnessing the principles of diffraction, DONNs execute complex computations through a single pass of light propagation with massive parallelism and minimal power consumption, offering a compelling alternative to conventional electronic architectures. In this review, we summarize the fundamental principles of DONNs and examine their applications across key domains, ranging from optical image classification and high-dimensional imaging to communication-capacity expansion through multiplexing and emerging uses in quantum information processing. Finally, we discuss the main challenges for practical implementation of DONNs and outline possible future directions for a new generation of intelligent systems that compute with light.
title: Diffractive optical neural networks for intelligent informatics: image processing, communications, and quantum applications

abstract: Diffractive neural networks (DNNs) are an emerging approach for the realization of photonic artificial intelligence, especially due to their suitability for machine-vision applications and high-dimensional photonic information processing at lower power consumption. However, incorporating optical nonlinear activation functions to make DNNs a feasible alternative to their electronic counterpart remains a challenge. Here, we investigate the inclusion of second-harmonic generation (SHG), as one of the simplest and most efficient types of optical nonlinearities, in DNNs. We numerically investigate the impact of SHG on the performance of classification tasks in an all-optical nonlinear DNNs. Specifically, we investigate and discuss the essential requirements for an effective arrangement of a SHG activation in single and multilayer DNNs. We find that the performance, in terms of classification accuracy and class contrast, is affected strongly by the positioning of the SHG activation. Finally, we discuss and outline the constraints for including SHG in an experimental realization. Taking these constraints into account, we estimate the power-related efficiency of the nonlinear DNN system. Overall, our results provide a path towards implementing nonlinear DNNs using the SHG process.
title: Second-harmonic generation for enhancing the performance of diffractive neural networks

abstract: Optical phased array (OPA)-based LiDAR technology provides high-speed, solid-state sensing for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and aerial systems. However, current OPA-based LiDAR platforms lack the ability to accurately recognize and classify materials, limiting their effectiveness for advanced scene understanding in robotics and machine perception. Here, we propose a method for OPA-based LiDAR that integrates a silicon photonic OPA chip with a polarisation-resolved optical neural network (PolarONN) chip to directly analyse the polarisation of backscattered signals. This integrated architecture enables a polarization-resolved point-cloud output by jointly providing 3D geometry, return intensity, and a polarization-derived attribute, and it attaches a point-wise material label inferred by the on-chip PolarONN. Compared to representative electronic classification back-ends used for polarization-based material identification, our on-chip photonic inference core provides ns-scale response with a low electrical power budget for the inference module. We experimentally demonstrate robust, real-time classification of three representative materials (wood, stone, and steel) with classification accuracies exceeding 85%, at distances up to 10 meters. Our study establishes a practical route toward real-time polarisation-resolved LiDAR perception, significantly enhancing the capabilities of next-generation autonomous sensing technologies. This study combines an optical phasedarray LiDAR with an integrated photonic neural network to map three-dimensional scenes and classify materials using polarization-resolved optical echoes.
title: Optical phased array LiDAR chips towards polarization-resolved 4D sensing
